messages:
Alex: Quick heads up — drafting internal release notes for v0.11.2. Planning internal announce at 16:00 PT today, public blast tomorrow 10:00 PT. Need ops + product + legal signoff by 15:00 PT.
Sam: Good. Can you paste the short blurb you intend to send so I can copycheck?
Alex: Sure — short blurb below (will also paste into /docs/releases/v0.11.2.md):
Alex: "Release v0.11.2 — runtime and serving fixes: improved continuous batching heuristics, KV cache stability fix, and Dedicated runtime pin to avoid kernel mismatch. Canary today, full rollout after green. No user-visible API changes."
Priya: Small ask: call out the Dedicated pin explicitly (customers + sales need that). Suggest: "Dedicated runtime pinned to 2026-03-21-rc3 to maintain deterministic latency profiles."
Jordan: Also add rollback heuristics in the note to ops: if 5m error rate delta > 1.5% OR latency P95 > 40% relative to baseline -> immediate rollback. Ops Oncall, can you ack that threshold?
Ops Oncall: Ack. Those thresholds sound reasonable. We'll also watch request_5xx_rate and model_token_errors. If either spikes, we escalate.
Sam: From comms: keep the blurb tight and include a link to the longer runbook. Something like: "See internal runbook: <https://infra/internal/runbooks/release-rollouts>"
Alex: Added. Also planning canary cadence: 10% for 20m, evaluate smoke eval, then ramp 30% over 15m, then full over 30m if stable.
Priya: Legal confirmation: these changes do not alter data retention or PII paths, correct?
Jordan: Correct, only serving runtime and batch planning; no customer data flow changes. Priya, please confirm.
Priya: Confirmed. No additional compliance notes.
Maya (deploybot): Scheduled deploy request received: `/deploy v0.11.2 --canary 10% --duration 20m` — queued by Alex. ETA: 2026-03-22T00:30:00Z.
Sam: Can we include the short deploy commands in the thread for ops? e.g.:
Sam: ```
# start canary
/deploy v0.11.2 --canary 10% --duration 20m
# rollback
/deploy rollback cb-7965432100
```
Ops Oncall: I'll standby at 15:30 PT and watch the canary. Luca will be primary oncall for this window.
Luca: Oncall acknowledged — I'll take the first watch and post live metrics.
Maya (deploybot): Canary started -> id=cb-7965432100, target 10% nodes, initiated by Alex.
Alex: Perfect. If smoke eval fails or metrics breach thresholds: immediate rollback command is `deploybot rollback cb-7965432100` or manual rollback via the runbook.
Jordan: One more: pin the model in the announce so customers aren't surprised. Add `model: redwood-v2.1-quant` to the note.
Alex: Done — added model pin and the dedicated runtime pin. Also added a short FYI for Sales & CS: "No breaking changes; pin may affect latency in edge cases — reach out to eng-ops for exemptions."
Sam: Wording tweak suggestion: swap to "May affect latency for pinned Dedicated pools; contact eng-ops for per-customer exemptions."
Alex: Accepted and updated.
Priya: Legal: ok to send internal blast.
Ops Oncall: I'll post live metrics link when the canary begins: https://metrics.internal/runs/cb-7965432100
Maya (deploybot): Canary health checks: initial probe OK on 3/3 nodes. Smoke eval job `ci/evals/canary-smoke` queued.
Alex: Final plan recap: internal announce at 16:00 PT with the short blurb + runbook link; canary now running (10% 20m) -> smoke eval -> ramp plan -> full roll if green. Rollback thresholds as stated. If anyone sees an issue, call `deploybot rollback cb-7965432100` and @Ops Oncall.
Sam: Approved from comms. Looks good to send when Alex posts.
Priya: Legal approved.
Jordan: Product approves.
Luca: I'll be watching and will post periodic updates in this thread during the rollout.
Alex: Thanks all — closing here, moving final copy to the internal-announce doc and scheduling the blast. :rocket:
